newsitem.title: UK: Ldn gold hovers above lows, PGMs nervously weaker.
newsitem.headline: Ldn gold hovers above lows, PGMs nervously weaker.

text.p: Gold prices edged just higher on Wednesday afternoon but the market was still hanging on by a thread above recent 12-year lows, dealers said.
The platinum group metals (PGMs) were also under pressure as the market anticipated long-delayed Russian deliveries to resume this week.

Gold was fixed at $317.30 an ounce, up on light short covering from $315.75 in the morning and $320.80 on Tuesday afternoon. Dealers said they expected gold to find some support at $313.60, the lowest in 12 years which was hit on Monday.
But further losses to the $300 level would probably be seen before any significant upside correction.

Prices nosedived last week after the Australian central bank announced it had sold 167 tonnes of gold from its reserves. The move was seen as the final straw for an already bearish market anxious about the prospect of central banks purging gold stocks.
The PGMs, meanwhile, were drifting lower as the market geared up for the arrival of Russian exports.
Japanese traders have said they were assured by Russian export officials that supplies would re-start on July 10 after being stalled since late last year by bureaucratic snarl-ups.
Russia is the world's biggest producer of palladium and second largest platinum producer after South Africa.
Platinum was trading at $395.00/$399.00, down $13 from Tuesday's London close, while palladium was off $7.00 at $167.00/$171.00.
Many traders said they expected prices to decline gradually, not plummet, once Russian material appeared on the market.
"Prices are being discounted now on expectation of deliveries. But I can't believe the first shipment going to have a huge effect on the price," a dealer said.
In the longer term, however, prices would continue to drop off from highs achieved in June at the peak of supply tightness.
"There's a big downside potential in the PGMs. It may not be to the February levels (from which the rally started) but I still expect to see a correction," a bullion analyst said.
Professionals were taking short positions for the latter part of the year rather than in the near term, he said.
Silver, taking its lead from gold, was trading in narrow range just above support at $4.25.
It was last indicated at $4.30/$4.32, down five cents from Tuesday's London close.
